date_scope_check.qualification_retained: REC50-R48-005-P1: In a December 26 interview, the Tunisian customs spokeswoman dates the temporary order to the previous night and normal restoration to noon on December 26. She attributes it to security information without specifying the threat. Al-Araby also reports that the Libyan side admitted returning nationals. Mosaïque’s dated December 26, 13:05 indexed report independently describes restoration at noon after the previous night’s stoppage; its correspondent attributes the episode to traders’ dispute with Libyan-side officials over seized goods, quoting the traders’ account. These are alternative attributed explanations, not a resolved common official motive. Mosaïque’s direct page remains inaccessible, although substantive article text is now recovered from the index. Exact clocks and exhaustive directions/exceptions remain unknown. One calendar-day difference does not establish 24 elapsed hours, and the overnight-to-noon accounts do not support a >24-hour classification. This episode is separate from the November–early December campaign.
